attempted_claim: Let Sigma_2 be the closed orientable surface of genus 2 and let F_n(Sigma_2) be its ordered n-point configuration space. Consider the integral FI-module n |-> H_2(F_n(Sigma_2); Z) with FI-morphisms on cohomology induced by forgetting points, in the Church-Ellenberg-Farb/Miller-Wilson framework where the generic closed-manifold bound gives generation degree at most 10. Decide whether this integral FI-module is generated in degree at most 6 with presentation degree at most 8, and decide whether its torsion subgroup has a uniform exponent dividing 2 for all n with an explicit eventual vanishing or non-vanishing threshold. A complete answer proves the explicit generation degree at most 6, presentation degree at most 8, and uniform 2-power torsion bound for all n, or rigorously disproves at least one of them by exhibiting a minimal integral 2-torsion class or an integral cycle in some F_n(Sigma_2) not induced from at most 6 points, via the puncture resolution and Gan-Li FI-hyperhomology bounds plus a small-n integral computation.
claim_type: improved integral generation/presentation degrees plus uniform torsion exponent
decisive_failure: The formal puncture-resolution plus Gan-Li route lacked exact genus-2 regularity inputs beyond the generic generation bound of 10; the bounded Totaro/Smith-normal-form computation provably accesses only H^2-fragments rather than H_2 torsion; the n=3 twisted Hochschild-Serre computation and explicit 2-torsion cycle search were not closable in this pass.
domain: integral representation stability of closed-surface configurations
